workout.warmup: The 15-min walk to PF is your warmup — that covers it. Heavy pressing still needs ramp-up sets on the Smith bench: 1 plate/side (45s) x 8, then 1 plate + a 25/side x 5. Then your work sets. Do not cold-open a heavy press.
workout.finisher: The walk home. No treadmill finisher needed while you're at this location.
workout.coach_note: Day 2 of the heavy block. Same rules as yesterday: main lifts go 4x5–6 with 2–3 min rest, accessories stay 10–15. Yesterday you learned the big lesson — 75 lb DBs and your grip are the ceiling at this PF, not your muscles. So the heavy press moves to the SMITH MACHINE where you can actually load it. Same logic as your deadlift idea — you were right, run Smith for the heavy hinge next lower day too. Straps should land in a couple days; that fixes RDL and hanging knee raises both.

exercises.name: Smith Machine Bench Press [HEAVY]
exercises.note:
MAIN LIFT. PLATE MATH, not a total — the PF Smith bar is angled and counterbalanced, so the naked bar is nowhere near 45 lb and nobody knows the real number. Ignore totals, count plates.

START: 2 plates/side (45+45). Ramp up first: 45/side x8, then 45+25/side x5.

READ THE FIRST WORK SET — same as you did on leg press today:
- Got 8+ → add a 10 per side, too light
- Got 5-6 hard but clean → that's the weight, stay for all 4 sets
- Got 3-4 → strip a 10 per side

Write down what you land on and it becomes the number going forward. Watch the left shoulder — if anything pinches, strip a 10 and stay there.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown [HEAVY]
exercises.note: MAIN LIFT. 125 gave you 10/8/10 on 7/11. Go to 150–160 and pull hard for 5–6. VERTICAL pull. Full stretch at the top, drive the elbows down and back. If your grip starts slipping before your lats give out, that's the strap problem again — note it and it's solved this week.

exercises.name: DB Shoulder Press [HEAVY]
exercises.note: MAIN LIFT. 45 lb gave you 10/9/10 — that's got room. Go to 60 lb for sets of 5–6. This is well under the 75 lb DB ceiling so you're fine here. Seated, back supported, press without flaring the elbows. Left shoulder has handled every jump so far — keep it honest and stop the set if the groove feels off.

exercises.name: Seated Cable Row (PF)
exercises.note: Accessory — stays in the volume range. 130 is your confirmed working weight from 7/11 (125 was easy, 130 gave you 10/10). Start at 130. HORIZONTAL pull, pairs with the pulldown above. Chest tall, squeeze at the back, no torso rocking.

exercises.name: Face Pulls
exercises.note: 60 worked at the last PF but machines vary location to location — gauge by first-set reps and land in the 12–15 zone. Elbows high and wide. Don't skip these; they're what's kept the shoulder trending the right way.

exercises.name: Arms Superset — Rope Pushdown + Cable Curl
exercises.detail: 80 lb both · 3 rounds x 10–12 · 60–75s between rounds
exercises.note: You ran both at 70 lb and got 12/12/11 on pushdowns and 12/12/12 on curls — curls especially were strong all the way through. Both go to 80 lb. Same cable stack, back to back, minimal rest inside the round.

exercises.name: Core Circuit — 2 rounds
exercises.detail: Cable Crunch x12 → Dead Bugs x10/side → Side Plank 45–60s/side
exercises.note: Rotated off yesterday's combo. No hanging work today — your grip is already getting taxed by the pulldown, and it's what cut your knee raises short yesterday. Side planks per your own note: you said 30s was too easy and you hit a full minute, so it's 45–60s/side now. Cable crunch: kneel, round INTO the crunch, don't just hip-hinge.
